fixes.explanation: That's the verdict, friend. The priest sees two things at once: the hair in the spot has turned white, and the sore appears deeper than the skin. Verse 3 says, “…it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.” I don't pull a batch out of the oven on a hunch either. I look first, and so does the priest.

A river trip? Nobody here is packing swim trunks, friend. Washing does come up in this chapter, but it's clothes (Leviticus 13:6, 34) or a mildewed article (Leviticus 13:54). None of it is the answer to this verdict. In verse 3 the priest examines the person and “…must pronounce him unclean.”

A cloth sounds sensible, like a tea towel over a cooling rack. But that's not the step in verse 33. There the person “…must shave himself except for the scaly area.” Then the priest isolates him for another seven days.

Harmless is the word, and it's good news. Verse 39 says, “…if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.” The priest looks, says clean, and I do a happy dance right here on my gold base. Dull white spots, harmless rash, clean.

BURN IT, baker! Verse 57 says, “But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.” The priest already tried cutting out the mildewed section in verse 56. When the mildew comes back, the text doesn't send him for a second snip. It says burn.
